doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Songs with Hampton and touring to Hawaii
summary: He sang Why Was I Born and Everybody's Somebody's Fool, and traveled widely including to Hawaii.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Did they discuss what material you would sing?

No. I sang, “Why was I born? Why am I living?” [Why was I born]. That was one of the features that he wanted me to do. And a couple of things he had me doing. Don’t take your love was one, and Everybody’s Somebody’s Fool, after we recorded it. That was one of them that I did. When I left the band, he tried to get the singers that he had to do the song, because the song was getting popular.
Everybody’s Somebody’s Fool. He couldn’t get anyone to do it, because they’re saying, no, that’s Jimmy’s song. We ain’t going to do that. Most of them were loyal in that sense. That was how it went.
How long of a period of time were you out there with Hampton? Did you travel all over the country?

Yes. We traveled many places. That’s the first time I got to Hawaii, was with his band. It was an overnight thing. When I woke up, I’m laying on the ground, on the grass, and they’re telling me, “Come on. Get up.” “Get up? Where am I?” I must be in Heaven somewhere.
Must be in Heaven; turned out to be Hawaii.

Yeah. That’s right. It turned out to be Hawaii. They entertained us that evening. Then we slept. Then they entertained us that night, before we left. Then we got the bus and left there and crossed all that water. They had a ship that took us across.
